acceptance: A write that exceeds the client timeout can be retried with the same operation id and reports the original outcome.
The timeout message names how to reconcile.
Measured p95 latency of take and finish recorded before and after.
context: BenchBox tracker store: BenchBox-dev/BenchBox branch todo-state. The host also had intermittent GitHub network drops the same day, which may explain the latency.
description:
Observed twice on 2026-11-12 against the BenchBox state store:
- `finish` on benchbox-lock-theseus-review-format-release-a-20261110 returned 'MCP failure … stage: receive, failure: timeout … Request timeout after 30000ms … the request outcome is unknown'. A later list_items showed the item done.
- `take` on theseus-review-minimize-superseded-20261110 timed out the same way. The item stayed open and unclaimed, and a retry took it.
In both cases the client cannot tell whether the write landed. A blind retry of finish would be refused or would double-apply, and a blind retry of take could fail with E_MULTIPLE_CLAIMS if the first had landed. Agents have to read the state back by hand.
Work (tractable product; owner decides where it is fixed):
- Return the operation id before the slow part, or make the MCP write timeout longer than the state-branch push time.
- Make every write idempotent under a client-supplied operation id, so a retry with the same id is safe.
- Document the reconcile step (`tractable recover --op-id`, or show_item) in the timeout message.
Guardrails: no hand edits of the state branch; changes go through the tractable repository's own review.
